Helpers stay short and plain after the prd split: generate.ts composes section builders instead of inlining them, job.ts keeps slug and entity helpers as small pure functions, and the extracted Header reads as straightforward JSX with no dense one-liners.
The prd and shell splits were driven by a measured size cap and a real second consumer, not by anticipated reuse. No interface was introduced with a single implementation for future flexibility.
The header split reuses the existing Breadcrumbs component, i18n bundle and theme tokens rather than adding copies, and the nav work introduced no new dependency.

The prd and shell refactors are pure structural moves. generatePrd output was verified byte-identical across five varied inputs by running the pre-split and post-split modules side by side, so the diff adds no behaviour of its own.
Handlers that read a request body run it through a schema before use; JSON.parse alone is not treated as validation anywhere under functions/.

This app ships no authentication surface, so there is no guard to stub: functions/lib holds only http and env helpers. Confirmed no auth-named function anywhere under functions/ returns an unconditional truthy value and no TODO-auth marker exists.

The refactor is covered by a characterization test snapshotting real generatePrd output for varied inputs, and the shell by a test querying header links by role. Both assert behaviour that breaks on regression rather than mere presence.
Tests assert rendered behaviour (header exposes named links by role, active route marked) and real output content, not implementation details or call counts.
Page.tsx is a composition of named components (Header, MobileDrawer, Footer, Breadcrumbs) rather than a monolithic shell, and pages supply title, subtitle and children into that shell.
The composer renders explicit loading, empty and error states. A failed submit surfaces an error rather than an empty success, and the empty thread says so in words instead of rendering blank.
